# Impact designer — distinctive production-grade frontend interfaces

Curated by Skill Harbor — @bencium's impact-designer skill (based on Anthropic's Frontend Designer skill): build distinctive, production-grade frontend interfaces that avoid generic "AI slop" aesthetics. Core philosophy: ask to understand context first (purpose, tone, constraints, what makes it unforgettable), then COMMIT BOLDLY to one aesthetic direction. Ships a huge tone-option menu (brutally minimal, retro-futuristic, brutalist, art deco, clay/soft 3D, cinematic noir, Nordic calm, museum exhibition, blueprint…), foundational design principles (distinctive typography — never Inter/Roboto/Arial/Space Grotesk by default; cohesive color with sharp accents; deliberate motion; unexpected spatial composition; atmospheric backgrounds), an anti-generic-patterns list (no SaaS blue, no purple gradients on white, no glass morphism, no "Claude-generated" look), inspiration sources (Awwwards, FWA, Codrops, studio references), creative reframing prompts ("What would Sagmeister do?", "What if this was a museum exhibit?"), an anti-sameness protocol (roll dice on color temperature, layout, type personality, motion, density), and an implementation checklist (gradient meshes, grain overlays, dramatic shadows, custom cursors). Honest caveats: guidance + creative process, no tooling — the agent writes the code; overlaps with other design listings here (anthropics frontend-design variants, cline-skills-frontend-design, affaan-m-ecc-frontend-design) — same craft, different authors. MIT...
